data.description:
Round-9 **major** defect, recorded in `content-management` but not owned by any rubric item — it is a defect in the front door and it costs the loop coverage every time it fires.

## The judge's own words

> **`/api/v1/auth/exchange` → `/signin?reason=expired`.** A fresh, never-used speaker magic sign-in link is consumed with no effect and the failure is misreported. Opening the just-issued `/api/v1/auth/exchange` link in a browser that already held another session redirected to `/signin?reason=expired` with "Link expired. That sign-in link had already been used or had passed its fifteen minutes." The link was neither used nor expired — the real cause was the pre-existing session.

## Why this is worth a ticket of its own

Two separate failures stacked, and the second is worse than the first:

1. **The link is burned.** A single-use credential was consumed by a request that did not sign anyone in. The person now has to request another one, and the product gave them no reason to expect that.
2. **The product blames the user for something it did.** "That sign-in link had already been used or had passed its fifteen minutes" is false in both clauses. The organizer or speaker reading it will re-request, hit the same pre-existing session, and get the same lie again — a loop with no exit that the copy actively steers them away from escaping, because nothing mentions the session they are already holding.

PHILOSOPHY.md's honesty rule lands squarely on this: the system knows exactly why it refused and it says something else.

It also matters operationally. Every eval scenario that signs in as a second identity in a browser that already holds a session walks into this, spends turns on it, and those turns are the same budget that has already cost us four unjudged items this round.

## What to build

1. **Do not consume the token on a path that cannot complete the sign-in.** If a pre-existing session blocks the exchange, the link must survive so the next attempt can use it.
2. **Say the true reason.** The message names the actual state — someone is already signed in — and distinguishes it from expiry and from re-use. Three different causes, three different sentences.
3. **Offer the way out.** The screen that reports it carries the action that resolves it: sign out of the current session and continue with this link, or continue as the person already signed in. A dead end here strands a real speaker at the door of their own portal.
4. Check the same reasoning for every consumer of a single-use token — a magic link, a resume token, an invite — so this is fixed once rather than three times.

## Acceptance

- Opening a fresh exchange link while another session exists does **not** invalidate the link; a retry after signing out succeeds with that same link.
- The failure states the real cause and is distinguishable from a genuinely expired and a genuinely re-used link.
- Regression test covers all three causes and asserts the fresh-link-survives property.

## Constraints

- Your **own linked worktree**, created as your first act, then `pwd` and `git branch --show-current` to prove it. Never the primary checkout (it is the Lattice board's home); never `mrq-auto-eval*`.
- **Never `git stash` anywhere in this repo** — the stash stack is shared across every worktree.
- **No migration without the operator.** If you conclude one is needed, stop and say so on the ticket.
- **Do not deploy.** An eval round is running and a `.deploy-freeze` marker sits at the primary checkout. Merging is wanted; deploying is not, and is not yours.
- **Elements never jump** — reserve space for anything that swaps.
- Ship a regression test that fails on `main` and passes on your branch.
- Gate serialized. macOS has no `flock(1)`; wrap it: `python3 -c 'import fcntl,subprocess,sys; f=open("/tmp/marquee-gate.lock","w"); fcntl.flock(f, fcntl.LOCK_EX); sys.exit(subprocess.run(["npm","run","pr-gate"]).returncode)'`
- PR: `gh pr create --repo Stage-11-Agentics/marquee --base main`.

data.body: Root cause: /api/v1/auth/exchange consumed a live magic link before checking the browser session, so the session conflict burned the token and was mislabeled as expired. Verified A/B: the CONTRACT · MRQ-181 regression failed on baseline d06f4319 with expected /portal to be /signin and passes on 54eef389bd34; /Users/atin/Projects/Stage11/deployments/Marquee-worktrees/.gate-lock/gate-lock.sh npm test exited 0 with status pass-over-budget, the same gate-lock command for npm run pr-gate returned status pass, and the exact-head Worker on port 8895 reported /health build 54eef389bd34, then returned /signin?reason=already_signed_in with the same token and /portal after logout. PR #217: https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/marquee/pull/217
